question: Who Owns Bojangles?
quick_answer: Bojangles is privately owned by two New York investment firms, Durational Capital Management and The Jordan Company, which took the chain private in a roughly $593 million deal in 2019. Bojangles was founded in 1977 in Charlotte, North Carolina, by Jack Fulk and Richard Thomas.
key_facts: Founders: Jack Fulk and Richard Thomas
Current owners: Durational Capital Management and The Jordan Company

body.heading: Who owns Bojangles?
body.text: Bojangles is owned by two New York-based investment firms, Durational Capital Management and The Jordan Company. In 2019 they acquired Bojangles in a deal worth about $593 million and took the company private, meaning its shares no longer trade on a stock exchange. It had previously been publicly listed on the NYSE under the ticker BOJA.

body.heading: How Bojangles started
body.text: Bojangles was founded in 1977 in Charlotte, North Carolina, by Jack Fulk and Richard Thomas. It built its name on Southern-style fried chicken, made-from-scratch buttermilk biscuits, seasoned fries and sweet tea, and grew into a major chain across the Southeast.

body.heading: What private ownership means
body.text: Going private in 2019 let Bojangles focus on long-term growth without the pressures of quarterly public reporting. Its owners have backed expansion into new markets. For customers, the menu and restaurants are unchanged by the ownership structure.
